The most significant revisions affect 2028–2030: capex forecasts are lowered by 28% for 2028 and by 41% and 40% for 2029 and 2030, respectively. Under the new model, global AI accelerator capex in 2030 falls to $923 billion from the previously projected $1.531 trillion—a reduction of $608 billion. Cumulative accelerator logic silicon wafer shipment area for 2026–2030 is cut by 17%, with Nvidia accounting for 66% of the reduction.

The revisions stem from three factors: slowing AI revenue growth, as frontier AI labs saw declining growth in new annual recurring revenue in Q3, prompting reassessment of whether token revenue can cover high computing costs; tighter financing conditions, with debt and equity investors more cautious about projects lacking long-term procurement commitments from cloud providers; and intensifying U.S. regulatory and grid-connection constraints, with 5.8 GW of data centers expected to come online between H2 2027 and H1 2028 facing delays.

The impact is uneven across the supply chain. LSA comes in two forms: D-LSA, which freezes a pretrained model and adds small projection matrices trained via distillation on 352M tokens, and N-LSA, trained natively from scratch with only next-token prediction and no added parameters.
